units.text: EXT. MANGROVE SWAMP - DUSK
Brackish water, knotted roots rising like fingers.
A small aluminum boat lies keel-up in the shallows, half sunk in silt.
Mosquitoes hang in veils.
RUTH ABERNETHY-SOLIS (50s, torn khakis, a field notebook held above the waterline) wades thigh-deep toward the wreck.
Behind her, her nephew KIERAN (20s, soaked, a coil of rope over his shoulder) hauls himself over a root.
A few paces further, a guide named TOMASI (60s, bare feet, a machete resting loosely at his side) watches the treeline.
Ruth reaches the boat.
Runs her palm along the hull.
Wipes the silt from a plate near the stern.
A stenciled name, scratched but legible: the same one as in her notebook.
She holds the notebook open beside it.
Compares.
Closes it without a word.
Kieran lowers the rope.
Tomasi turns his head.
Far off, something large moves through the water, rippling the surface in a long slow V.
None of them speaks.
Ruth tucks the notebook inside her shirt.
Kieran steps closer to her.
Tomasi lifts the machete, a few inches, and holds it there.
The ripple vanishes.
The mosquitoes whine.
Ruth nods once, and the three of them begin to wade, very carefully, back the way they came.
